svg.title: Occurrence, relations, and reflective minimization
svg.desc: Seven portrait frames form a fan around a separated central frame labeled Momentary epistemic minimum. Arcs connect the frames. Points on those arcs lead to difference, retention, and mutual constraint as relational conditions necessary for inference. Reflective minimization identifies the central occurrence as an epistemic limit point. The relations are not claimed to suffice for inference. The time axis is a schematic inferential model, not a claim that the minimum directly establishes time or independent minimal entities.

text.tspan: Distinguish the relations inference requires from its reflective identification of the epistemic minimum.
The domain of concepts, inference, and justification
Evidence, coherence, explanatory power, prediction, and successful intervention
The work of supporting and revising
World, subject, and value models are revised in relation to one another
Meta-judgment: “Present occurrence is the epistemic minimum”
This identification and its articulation also belong within concepts and inference
The relational structure that makes inference possible
Inference requires relations, not merely the existence of individual moments.
Relational structure is shown as necessary; it is not claimed to be sufficient for inference.
Time is schematic within an inferential model; the frames do not assert a series of independent minimal entities.
